chapterTitle: Unit 12: Angle in a Segment of a Circle
subject: math-10

questions.question: The measure of a central angle of a minor arc of a circle is:

options.A: Double the angle subtended by the corresponding major arc at the circumference
options.B: Equal to the angle subtended at the circumference
options.C: Half of the angle subtended at the circumference

questions.explanation: Theorem 1 of Unit 12: Central Angle = 2 × Inscribed Angle subtended by the same arc.

questions.question: If the central angle subtended by an arc is 80°, the angle subtended by the same arc at the circumference is:
questions.explanation: Inscribed angle = (Central angle) / 2 = 80° / 2 = 40°.

questions.question: Any two angles in the same segment of a circle are:
questions.explanation: Theorem 2 of Unit 12: Angles subtended by the same arc in the same segment are equal.

questions.question: The angle inscribed in a semicircle is a:
questions.explanation: Theorem 3: Since the central angle of a semicircle is 180°, the inscribed angle is 180° / 2 = 90° (Thales' theorem).

questions.question: The angle in a segment greater than a semicircle (major segment) is:
questions.explanation: The central angle of a minor arc is < 180°, so the inscribed angle is < 90° (acute).

questions.question: The angle in a segment less than a semicircle (minor segment) is:
questions.explanation: The central angle of a major arc is > 180°, so the inscribed angle in the minor segment is > 90° (obtuse).

questions.question: The opposite angles of any cyclic quadrilateral are:
questions.explanation: Theorem 4: In any cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite interior angles is always 180°.

questions.question: If ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and ∠A = 70°, then ∠C is:
questions.explanation: Opposite angles are supplementary: ∠C = 180° - ∠A = 180° - 70° = 110°.

questions.question: If ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and ∠B = 105°, then ∠D is:
An angle subtended by an arc at the centre is called a/an:
questions.explanation: An angle whose vertex is the centre of the circle is defined as a central angle.

questions.question: An angle whose vertex lies on the circumference of a circle and whose arms contain chords is a/an:
questions.explanation: An angle formed by two chords meeting at a point on the circumference is an inscribed angle.

questions.question: If an inscribed angle is 55°, the central angle subtended by the same arc is:
questions.explanation: Central angle = 2 × Inscribed angle = 2 × 55° = 110°.

questions.question: In a cyclic quadrilateral, if an exterior angle is formed by producing one side, it is equal to the:
questions.explanation: Since interior + exterior = 180° and interior + opposite = 180°, the exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle.

questions.question: A quadrilateral whose all four vertices lie on a circle is called a:
questions.explanation: A polygon whose vertices all lie on a common circle is cyclic (concyclic points).

questions.question: Can a non-rectangular parallelogram be cyclic?

options.A: No, because opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so for a cyclic one they must both be 90° (a rectangle)
options.C: Only if it is a rhombus with angles 60° and 120°

questions.explanation: In a parallelogram opposite angles are equal (x = y). In cyclic, x + y = 180° ⟹ 2x = 180° ⟹ x = 90°, so it must be a rectangle.

questions.question: A cyclic parallelogram is necessarily a:
questions.explanation: A parallelogram inscribed in a circle must have all angles equal to 90°, making it a rectangle.

questions.question: A cyclic rhombus is necessarily a:
questions.explanation: A rhombus has equal sides; being cyclic forces its angles to be 90°, making it a square.

questions.question: If triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle with side BC as diameter, then ∠BAC is:
questions.explanation: An angle inscribed in a semicircle with diameter BC is always a right angle (90°).

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, if minor arc AB subtends ∠AOB = 100°, then the reflex angle ∠AOB is:
questions.explanation: Reflex angle = 360° - 100° = 260°.

questions.question: Points that all lie on the circumference of the same circle are called:
questions.explanation: Points through which a single circle passes are defined as concyclic points.
